teacher shortage = a lack of qualified staff to fill teaching posts
class size = the number of pupils taught together in one group
flipped classroom = a method where students study content at home and practise in class
inquiry-based learning = a method in which pupils investigate questions rather than only receiving facts
e-learning = study that uses digital platforms as the main medium
MOOC = a free or low-cost online course open to very large numbers of learners
lifelong learning = continuing to study and retrain throughout adult life
adult education = organised learning for people who have left full-time school
continuing professional development = ongoing training that keeps practitioners' skills up to date
learner-centred = designed around students' needs and activity rather than only the teacher's talk
educational inequality = unfair differences in access, quality or outcomes of schooling
attainment gap = the difference in exam results between groups of pupils
homework gap = unequal ability to study at home because of missing devices, internet or space
disadvantaged background = growing up with fewer financial, educational or social resources
elite education = schooling that is highly selective, expensive or socially exclusive
school funding = the money provided to run schools, from the state or other sources
widening participation = policies that help under-represented groups enter higher education
private tuition = paid one-to-one or small-group teaching outside school
dropout rate = the share of students who leave a course before finishing
pupil premium = extra state money in England for schools with disadvantaged pupils
